validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE + SPEC: Read both of the sheet's own cited youm7.com articles in full (not just the snippet). 2019 article (https://www.youm7.com/story/2019/5/26/.../4257527), item 15 of a numbered Ministry-of-Petroleum project list: من المخطط تنفيذ ازدواج خط منتجات المنيا / أسيوط بطول 115 كم لرفع معدلات نقل المنتجات البترولية إلى المنيا وأسيوط إلى 8 آلاف طن يومياً ('planned: duplication of the El Minya/Asyut products line, 115 km, to raise transport rates to Minya and Asyut to 8,000 tons/day') -- status PLANNED as of 2019, length 115 km. NOTE: the same article's item 14, immediately before it, is a DIFFERENT 115 km line (Sokhna/El-Tebin, connecting Upper Egypt lines to the Sokhna area) -- confirmed the 115 km figure attaches to the Minya/Asyut item, not a mixup with the Sokhna-Tebin project (which is P7321). 2022 article (.../5810383), listed among 'the most prominent line projects that have been inaugurated': مشروع ازدواج خط نقل المنتجات البترولية (المنيا – أسيوط) بطول 115 كم ('project to double the petroleum-products transport line (El Minya - Asyut), 115 km') -- now COMPLETED/inaugurated, same 115 km. This is a clean planned(2019)->completed(2022) lifecycle match on length, corridor and commodity, which corroborates GEM's LengthKnown=115.00 km, Status=operating, Fuel='Oil products (only)', PipelineType='transmission', StartState/Province=El Minya, EndState/Province=Asyut all at once. CAVEAT: both citations are the same outlet (youm7.com) relaying what reads as the same Ministry of Petroleum reporting cycle at two dates -- I could not find a second, differently-sourced outlet corroborating this specific 115 km duplication project (WebSearch was unavailable this session -- budget exhausted at 200/200 calls before I could search, per the session-wide constraint already logged for other countries in this sweep; petroleum.gov.eg, Egypt Oil & Gas, Al-Borsa etc. were not checked). Tier is therefore medium rather than high on a strict same-origin reading, though the two dated snapshots (target -> delivered) give real corroborative value beyond a single restatement. DIAMETER/CAPACITY: neither article gives a pipe diameter; the 2019 article's '8,000 tons/day' figure is a stated corridor-wide TARGET transport rate for Minya+Asyut after duplication, not an explicitly stated single-pipe capacity spec, so I did not stage it as a Capacity fill (too much unit/attribution ambiguity -- tons/day vs GEM's typical bbl/d, and whether it means this pipe alone or the corridor). Left Diameter and Capacity blank rather than force a number. CLASSIFICATION: 'Oil products (only)' and PipelineType='transmission' both match the sourced description (a long-haul petroleum-products transport line between two governorates) -- no reclassification needed.

validity.researcher_notes: DUPLICATE WATCHLIST QUESTION -- P7316 'El Minya-Asyut Oil Pipeline' (140 km, dia 16 in, construction) vs P7342 'El Minya-Asyut Oil Products Pipeline' (115 km, dia blank, operating). Checked P7316's own harvested wiki citations (wiki_citations.json['pages']['P7316']): its sources are a 2024 youm7.com article headlined by the Petroleum Minister on the 'national CRUDE-oil handling/transport network' (الشبكة القومية لتداول الخام, 'national network for handling crude') and a 2021 article about a bank financing infrastructure/pipeline projects -- entirely different commodity framing (crude) and citation base from P7342's PRODUCTS-line duplication story. Different length (140 vs 115 km), different diameter (16 in vs unstated), different status (construction vs operating), different commodity emphasis (crude vs refined products), and no overlapping citation. This reads as two distinct, independently-documented physical pipelines sharing the same Minya-Asyut corridor name, not a double-count. No merge recommended; each row should keep its own sourcing.
